messages:
maria: Heads-up: production rollout v2.5.4 canary (usw2) is showing decoder errors + latency. p95 decode time spiked to ~2.1s and error rate ~0.7% over the last 5m. I recommend a manual rollback to v2.5.3 and locking the change window. :eyes:

chris: Can you paste the canary job id and the error logs? Any impact on embeddings or only text gen?

maria: canary id: canary-1825-prod-usw2. Logs: linked in thread (perf graphs). No embeddings regression — only long-prompt text gen path. Stack traces point at attention-kernel fallback.

deploy-bot: ALERT: Auto-rollback threshold breached (latency_p95 > 1.8s) for canary-1825-prod-usw2 at 2026-11-02T14:12:03Z. Suggested action: manual rollback or pin.

devops-oncall: Plan proposal:
1) pin prod traffic to v2.5.3 via traffic-split
2) run `deploy rollback --to v2.5.3 --env prod --graceful`
3) monitor p95 + error rate for 10 minutes
4) update incident channel + status page + customer comms
Whoever runs step 2 please ack with :white_check_mark:.

jake: I'll do the traffic pin and execute rollback in 2m. Commands I'm going to run:
```
redwoodctl traffic set prod --route default --version v2.5.3 --weight 100
redwoodctl deploy rollback --to v2.5.3 --env prod --no-canary
```

tanya: Are there customers we should proactively notify (long-prompt customers)? Recommend drafting an outbound to customers@ and a short blurb for status.redwood.com: 'Detected latency regression in recent release; rolled back to v2.5.3; monitoring.' Legal/CS ok?

maria: Agreed. I'll loop in Legal for wording. Also locking the change window until 04:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: ACTION: Rollback job started by jake at 2026-11-02T14:16:10Z. JobID: rb-5599. Estimated duration: ~3m.

jake: Rollback completed. Verified traffic now pinned to v2.5.3. p95 back to 0.85s, errors down to 0.03%. :thumbsup:

devops-oncall: Monitoring for 10m — initial 5m looks stable. Emily, can you run a smoke pass on customer QA tenants and confirm?

emily: Running smoke now against 10 tenants. All checks green.

tanya: I'll post the incident note and queue the customer outbound. Drafted message looks good, will send after legal OK.

maria: Thanks everyone. Postmortem next steps: collect prompt traces for failing requests, compare kernel selection and quantization paths between 2.5.4 and 2.5.3, add a rollout checklist item to validate long-prompt decoder kernels. Assign eng-runtime to investigate.

chris: tagging eng-runtime leads @andrew @sam for investigation. Also add a flag in release checklist to opt-out new kernel heuristics behind a feature toggle.

maria: Closing this thread once postmortem plan is in docs and customer comms sent. Good work — nice quick execution. :white_check_mark:
